content: 1. Aluminum hydroxide, magnesium hydroxide, and simethicone can be taken orally in a dose of 10-20 mL every 4-6 hours, either 1 hour before or 3 hours after meals. Alternatively, 2-4 chewable tablets can be taken every 4-6 hours, but the total should not exceed 12 tablets in 24 hours. The safety and efficacy of this regimen have not been established. 2. Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, which reduces the absorption and effectiveness of pazopanib. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated. If necessary, short-acting antacids may be used instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) or H2 antagonists, but antacid and pazopanib doses should be separated by several hours. 3. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of raltegravir by binding to cations in the gastrointestinal tract. Co-administration is contraindicated, and dose separation does not mitigate this interaction. 4. Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, which decreases the solubility and plasma concentrations of atazanavir. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Atazanavir should be administered 2 hours before or 1 hour after aluminum hydroxide-containing medications. 5. Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide reduce the absorption of baloxavir marboxil by binding to polyvalent cations in the gastrointestinal tract. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Studies in monkeys have shown significantly reduced plasma levels when baloxavir is taken with calcium, aluminum, or iron. Human studies have not been conducted. 6. Aluminum hydroxide reduces ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Ciprofloxacin should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide-containing products. 7. Magnesium hydroxide reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 8. Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, which reduces the absorption and effectiveness of dapsone. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 9. Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, which reduces the absorption and effectiveness of dasatinib. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 10. Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, which enhances the absorption of digoxin. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 11. Magnesium hydroxide reduces doxycycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Doxycycline should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium hydroxide-containing products. 12. Aluminum hydroxide reduces eltrombopag levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated, and doses should be separated by at least 4 hours. 13. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of fleroxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Fleroxacin should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide-containing products. 14. Simethicone reduces the absorption and effectiveness of infigratinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. If co-administration cannot be avoided, infigratinib should be administered 2 hours before and after locally-acting antacids. 15. Aluminum hydroxide reduces gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Gemifloxacin should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide-containing products. 16. Simethicone reduces the absorption and effectiveness of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. If co-administration cannot be avoided, sotorasib should be administered 4 hours before or 10 hours after locally-acting antacids. 17. Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, which reduces the solubility and plasma concentrations of acalabrutinib. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Doses should be separated by at least 2 hours. 18. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of acebutolol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Acebutolol should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide-containing products. 19. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of alendronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alendronate should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide-containing products. 20. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of allopurinol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Allopurinol should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide-containing products. 21. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of amphetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Co-administration should be monitored closely. 22. Aluminum hydroxide reduces atenolol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Atenolol should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide-containing products. 23. Aluminum hydroxide reduces azithromycin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Azithromycin should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide-containing products. 24. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of bearberry by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Co-administration should be monitored closely. 25. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of benazepril by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Co-administration should be monitored closely. 26. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of benzphetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Co-administration should be monitored closely. 27. Aluminum hydroxide reduces betaxolol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Betaxolol should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide-containing products. 28. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of bicalutamide by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Bicalutamide should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide-containing products. 29. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of bisoprolol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Bisoprolol should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide-containing products. 30. Magnesium hydroxide reduces cabotegravir levels by binding to cations in the gastrointestinal tract. Cabotegravir should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after magnesium hydroxide-containing products.
